findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on missing file, permission error, or I/O failure instead of returning a typed error
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file path aborts the entire request with a panic instead of a recoverable ParseError::Io
findings.fix: use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e))? and propagate a typed error enum

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value or empty field instead of returning a typed error
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV input like 'name,abc' aborts the request with a panic instead of returning ParseError::Invalid
findings.fix: replace with .parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| ParseError::Invalid(format!("bad value for '{}'" , parts[1])))?

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds side-channel I/O (stdout logging) inside what should be pure data-loading logic
findings.failure_mode: caller cannot suppress or capture debug output; stdout pollution breaks pipelines and leaks internal state
findings.fix: remove println!; move any debug logging to the shell boundary as a separate action with an injected logger trait

findings.problem: as u16 silently truncates any u32 value exceeding 65535, converting valid 32-bit data to a wrong value without error
findings.failure_mode: a file containing 'name,70000' silently produces Record { name, value: 4460 } instead of failing with an overflow error

findings.problem: parts[1] is unchecked indexing into a Vec<String> produced from line.split(',').collect() without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: a line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields (e.g., 'name_only') panics with index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: check parts.len() >= 2 before access, or use parts.get(1).ok_or(ParseError::Invalid("missing value field"))?

findings.problem: parts[0] is unchecked indexing without verifying the split produced any elements
findings.failure_mode: an empty line causes index-out-of-bounds panic
findings.fix: skip empty lines or check parts.first().ok_or(ParseError::Empty)?

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() allocates an intermediate Vec<String> instead of using the mandatory split_once for single-separator grammars
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary allocation on every line; split_once is required by the skill to parse name-value pairs with a single separator and avoid collecting intermediate vectors
findings.fix: let (_name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid("expected name,value"))?; then parse value_str.trim()

findings.problem: load_frames fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), domain construction (Record), stdout logging (println!), allocation (collect into Vec), and error handling (unwrap) into a single function
findings.failure_mode: violates Data/Calculations/Actions architecture; pure calculation logic is mixed with imperative shell I/O; shell cannot inject mock data or logger; no bounded allocation with try_reserve
findings.fix: split into: (1) shell function reads file and passes lines to (2) pure parse_records(lines: &[&str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> with try_reserve and no I/O

findings.problem: raw String and u16 primitives cross the parse boundary directly into domain struct Record without fallible smart constructors; callers can construct invalid domain states with any name string and any u16 value
findings.failure_mode: no invariant enforcement on name (no length, character, or format rules) and no validation that u16 value was produced through a checked parse path
findings.fix: define newtypes Name(String) and validated Value(u16) with smart constructors returning typed errors; Record should own these, not raw primitives

findings.problem: no benchmark, profiler, or allocation evidence exists for the load_frames function; performance claims cannot be verified
findings.failure_mode: unbounded allocation via Vec::collect() without try_reserve or domain cap; no measured baseline to justify the Vec<String> intermediate collection pattern
findings.fix: add a benchmark measuring allocations for typical input sizes; add try_reserve with a domain cap before the collect

findings.problem: no [dev-dependencies] for criterion or other benchmarking framework; no test binary; no canonical test gate exists
findings.failure_mode: cannot verify correctness or performance of load_frames without a test harness or benchmark infrastructure
findings.fix: add criterion or similar to dev-dependencies and write at least a basic test covering valid, empty, and malformed input

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_frames allocation or throughput behavior
no profiler data to identify hot paths or allocation hotspots
no allocation budget or try_reserve usage in production path
no second-ring evidence (command output) for any performance claim
no test binary or behavior tests exist for load_frames
residual_risk: Review is static-only with no commands executed. The crate contains 8 blocker-level violations including panic surfaces (unwrap), unchecked indexing, lossy casts, hidden I/O, missing split_once usage, functional core separation failure, absent parse boundary validation, and missing bounded allocation. All blockers must be fixed and re-reviewed before delivery. Without running cargo check/clippy/test, there is residual risk of undiscovered clippy warnings, type errors, or test failures.
